_comment: Boeing 777-200LR top-level design REQUIREMENTS -- what the aircraft must DO, fidelity-independent. Read the same way as f16a_requirements.json. SCOPE GUARD: requirements only, never spec data (reference area, AR, thrust, engine model stay in examples/B777/inputs/b777_L1.json) and never discipline-owned quantities (CLmax, CD0, K1, thrust-lapse alpha, TSFC come from the injected B777AeroL1 / B777PropL1 objects at run time). Each constraint row carries only its config string; the aero object supplies that config's polar and CLmax through aero.get_config_polar (the AerodynamicsBase contract). Full docs + per-field citations: examples/B777/inputs/b777_requirements.md.
_cite: metabook = AE481 metabook worked Example 4.2, docs/reference_extracts/metabook_data.md; Roskam Table 3.1 etc. are the primary tables the metabook names. Constraint-class field names verified against src/constraints/{TakeoffFieldLengthConstraint, LandingFieldLengthConstraint, ClimbGradientConstraint, ExcessPowerConstraint, LevelFlightConstraint}.m fromCondition readers.

cruise._src: cruise condition [metabook §4.11 Eq. 4.57] -- 40000 ft, M 0.84 (q = 228.8 lbf/ft2). Consumed by the mission long_range cruise segment and the Cruise constraint.

_src_design_range_nmi: Design mission range 9,150 nmi [metabook Example 2.1 requirement]. With the Example 2.1 payload (78,821 lbf = 14 crew + 314 pax x 109 kg) the metabook L1 closure sizes near the actual 777-200LR (MTOW 766,800 lbf, OEW 320,000 lbf) -- the lower payload offsets the longer range vs the earlier 6,000 nmi / 145,000 lbf stand-in.

constraints._comment: The ~10 B777 constraint conditions. Each object holds REQUIREMENT / CONDITION data ONLY. NO discipline-owned quantity is present: CLmax/CD0/K1 come from the injected B777AeroL1 object for the row's config string (via aero.get_config_polar), thrust-lapse alpha and TSFC from the injected B777PropL1 object, and n_engines (OEI factor) from the injected prop object. Unlike the F-16 set, most field/climb rows do NOT carry beta -- the metabook field and climb equations use explicit weight_ratio corrections. Only Ceiling (ExcessPowerConstraint) and Cruise (LevelFlightConstraint) carry beta, because those Master-Equation classes require it. Condition name -> concrete class is chosen explicitly by the future B777ConstraintSet map (implementation phase). See b777_requirements.md §§2-3.
constraints._cite: metabook = AE481 metabook worked Example 4.2, docs/reference_extracts/metabook_data.md.
constraints._note_field_length_classes: The B777 uses the FAR-25 STATISTICAL field-length classes (TakeoffFieldLengthConstraint / LandingFieldLengthConstraint, metabook Eqs. 4.14-4.19/4.45-4.48), NOT the Mattingly/Roskam ground-roll siblings the F-16 uses. See b777_requirements.md §2.2.
constraints._note_climb_CLmax: The six climb rows read CD0/K1/CLmax LIVE from the aero object for cond.config -- the config-CLmax basis (D1/D2, RESOLVED 2026-08-13 in favour of the printed values for parity) is produced by B777AeroL1 from the shared toolboxes (D10: Cfe = AeroL2.lookup_Cfe; per-config e/Delta_CD0 = AeroL1.Delta_CD0 upper bound [Roskam Table 3.6]), NOT stored in JSON. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Takeoff Field Length
conditions._src: TakeoffFieldLengthConstraint.fromCondition reads BFL_ft and the takeoff-field condition (altitude_ft; sigma = rho/rhoSL derived from that state). BFL_ft [metabook Eq. 4.47, TOP = 12000/37.5 = 320]. sigma [metabook Eq. 4.48, hot day near sea level rho/rhoSL = 0.95]: this ISA-only framework represents the hot day as the matching DENSITY ALTITUDE -- AircraftState(1742.4 ft) has sigma = 0.95000, reproducing the metabook denominator constant 0.95*320 = 304.0. CLmax_TO read live from aero 'takeoff_flaps_gear_down'. See b777_requirements.md §3.1.

conditions.name: Landing Field Length
conditions._src: LandingFieldLengthConstraint.fromCondition reads runway_ft, Sa_ft, weight_ratio, the landing-field condition (altitude_ft; sigma = rho/rhoSL derived from that state), optional runway_factor (defaults 0.6). All [metabook Eq. 4.46]: runway_ft = S_runway; Sa_ft = airliner approach distance [Eq. 4.19]; weight_ratio = MLW/MTOW for the 777-200LR; sigma = hot day near sea level, represented as density altitude AircraftState(1742.4 ft) = sigma 0.95000; runway_factor = FAR landing-field multiple (0.6 = 1/1.67). CLmax_L read live from aero 'landing_flaps_gear_down'. See b777_requirements.md §3.2.

conditions.name: Climb 1 (takeoff, FAR 25.111)
conditions._src: ClimbGradientConstraint.fromCondition reads G, ks, config, optional oei/hot_day/max_continuous/weight_ratio [metabook Eq. 4.49]. altitude_ft informational. oei factor N/(N-1) uses n_engines from the injected prop object. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Climb 2 (transition, FAR 25.121)
conditions._src: ClimbGradientConstraint [metabook Eq. 4.50]. altitude_ft informational. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Climb 3 (2nd segment, FAR 25.121)
conditions._src: ClimbGradientConstraint [metabook Eq. 4.51]. altitude_ft informational. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Climb 4 (enroute, FAR 25.121)
conditions._src: ClimbGradientConstraint [metabook Eq. 4.52]. Only max_continuous = true row (1/0.94 factor) and only clean-config row (flaps + gear retracted). altitude_ft informational. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Climb 5 (AEO balked landing, FAR 25.119)
conditions._src: ClimbGradientConstraint [metabook Eq. 4.53]. AEO (all-engines-operating) balked landing -- oei = false. weight_ratio = 0.65 (MLW/MTOW). altitude_ft informational. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Climb 6 (OEI balked landing, FAR 25.121)
conditions._src: ClimbGradientConstraint [metabook Eq. 4.54]. approach config: CD0 = 0.08847 = mean(0.06097, 0.11597), CLmax = 0.85*2.6 = 2.21 (from the aero object). weight_ratio = 0.65 (MLW/MTOW). altitude_ft informational. See b777_requirements.md §3.3.

conditions.name: Ceiling
conditions._src: CeilingConstraint.fromCondition reads altitude_ft, mach, G, power_setting. Service ceiling: minimum-T/W form T_SL/W = (1/alpha)*(2*sqrt(CD0*K1)+G) [metabook Eq. 4.30/4.56] -- a HORIZONTAL line (W/S-independent), NOT the W/S-dependent ExcessPower U-curve. G = 0.001 residual climb gradient [metabook Eq. 4.56]. power_setting = max (high-BPR transport rating set {cont,TO,max}; the metabook ceiling Eq. 4.56 uses full sigma^0.6 lapse, so 'max', not the derated 'cont'). See b777_requirements.md.
conditions._TODO_mach: ceiling mach = 0.84 stand-in (= cruise Mach; the metabook prints no ceiling Mach). Sets the drag polar / thrust lapse condition. Remove when pinned.
conditions._note_parity: CeilingConstraint uses ISA thrust lapse from AircraftState (alpha=sigma^m at 42000 ft, sigma_ISA=0.2236) vs the metabook's printed off-ISA alpha=0.2331^0.6 (sigma=0.2331 = ISA at ~41135 ft). ~2% gap (D5). Comparison report evaluates the printed Eq. 4.56 for parity.

conditions.name: Cruise
conditions._src: LevelFlightConstraint.fromCondition reads altitude_ft, mach, beta, power_setting (n = 1, Ps = 0 fixed by the class). altitude_ft, mach [metabook Eq. 4.57, q = 228.8 lbf/ft2]; beta = 1.0 (Master-Equation classes require beta; take W/W_TO = 1.0 unless a cruise-start fraction is specified as a requirement); power_setting = max (high-BPR transport rating set {cont,TO,max}; metabook cruise Eq. 4.57 uses full sigma^0.6 lapse). The framework uses ISA lapse rather than the printed 0.2846 ratio (D5). See b777_requirements.md §3.5.

missions._comment: Mission PROFILES: the ordered segment sequence each mission flies -- a REQUIREMENT, fidelity-independent. The B777 has one mission, long_range: a standard transport profile [metabook §2 / Algorithm 3; Roskam Table 3.4 historical fractions where a physics equation does not apply]. Each segment carries the MINIMUM per-segment inputs: type, end flight condition (alt_ft/mach_end), and whichever of distance_nm / time_min applies. NO discipline-owned data (CLmax, CD0, K1, thrust, TSFC come from the injected aero/prop objects) and NO spec data. See b777_requirements.md §5.
missions._cite: metabook = AE481 metabook Example 4.2 / §2, docs/reference_extracts/metabook_data.md; Raymer Table 3.4 historical weight fractions; metabook Eq. 2.7 (Breguet cruise), Eq. 2.17 (reserve).
missions._note_implementation_flag: A transport FIXED-FRACTION MissionEquations entry (Raymer Table 3.4 fractions + metabook Eq. 2.7 cruise + Eq. 2.17 reserve) is NOT yet in the repo's MissionEquations and must be added in the implementation phase before this mission runs. Code change, not a JSON input -- flagged so it is not missed. See b777_requirements.md §5.4.

long_range._description: metabook Example 2.1 long-range mission: startup/taxi/takeoff (folded historical 0.970), climb (0.985), cruise 9,150 nmi (Breguet Eq. 2.7), 30-min loiter (Breguet endurance Eq. 2.16), descent (0.990), landing/taxi (0.995). The 6% reserve_fuel_fraction [Eq. 2.17] (trapped fuel + additional reserve) is applied ON TOP of the full mission by MissionAnalysisBase -- it is separate from the 30-min design loiter above, so there is no double-count. Every physics/historical segment yields a fuel burn.
long_range._cite_reserve_fuel_fraction: Wf/W0 = (1 - W_final/W0)*1.06 [metabook Eq. 2.17] -- the 6% covers reserve and trapped fuel. See b777_requirements.md §5.3.
long_range._src_cruise_distance_nm: Cruise range = 9,150 nmi [metabook Example 2.1 mission requirement]. cruise Mach 0.84 and altitude 40,000 ft [metabook Eq. 4.57]. See b777_requirements.md §5.2.
long_range._src_loiter: 30-minute reserve loiter [metabook Example 2.1 mission requirement], a BreguetEnduranceSegment (Eq. 2.16) at the injected TSFC/L-over-D. Loiter altitude 5,000 ft / Mach 0.40 is a reasonable hold condition (Example 2.1 does not pin it) -- the 30-min leg burns ~1.3% of gross weight, so the condition barely moves the closure. The 6% reserve_fuel_fraction (Eq. 2.17, trapped fuel + additional reserve) still applies ON TOP of the full mission (loiter included), matching the metabook markup convention. See b777_requirements.md §5.2/§5.3.
long_range._note_takeoff_climb_mach_end: mach_end on the takeoff/climb segments = 0.84 is the cruise Mach used as the climb terminal condition; the metabook Example 4.2 fixed-fraction profile does not print intermediate Mach waypoints (startup/climb/descent/landing use Raymer Table 3.4 historical fractions, not a physics Mach). Carried for schema completeness. See b777_requirements.md §5.1.
